concerns.text: The plan states "Collect human feasibility scores for **all 1 000 prompts** (FR‑001 & FR‑009 reconciled)" (lines 2‑4). This directly conflicts with FR‑009, which only requires human scores for **at least 200 prompts**. If only 200 are annotated, the paired statistical tests on the 500 conflicting prompts will be under‑powered, violating the power analysis (Section 7) that assumes 500 annotated conflicting samples. The inconsistency undermines the methodological validity of the study.

The plan does not specify any randomization or counterbalancing of the order in which the baseline, graph‑augmented, and control conditions are presented to the verifier. Without randomizing condition order, there is a risk of order effects (e.g., model state carry‑over, caching) confounding the observed performance differences.

concerns.location: plan.md:Section 3 – Baseline Verifier Evaluation (FR‑003) / research.md:Section 9 – GPU Escape Hatch Note
concerns.text: The plan relies on a ‘GPU escape hatch’ (Kaggle free GPU) for the 1 B‑parameter Edit‑R1 verifier because the model exceeds the 7 GB RAM limit on a CPU‑only runner. This violates the project’s free‑compute constraint: all steps must be runnable on the GitHub Actions free‑tier runner (2 CPU cores, ≤ 7 GB RAM) without external paid or out‑of‑scope resources. Consequently the baseline verifier runtime budget (≤ 2 h) and overall ≤ 6 h wall‑clock limit are unrealistic on CPU alone, making the pipeline infeasible as written.

Section 1 of research.md states that human feasibility scores will be collected for **all 1 000 prompts** (\"Collect human feasibility scores for **all 1 000 prompts** (FR‑001 & FR‑009 reconciled)\"), while the specification (FR‑009) only requires scores for **at least 200 prompts**. The power analysis (Section 7) assumes 500 conflicting samples with human scores, yielding >0.8 power. If only 200 prompts receive human annotations, the paired test will be under‑powered, violating the claimed statistical power and potentially leading to false‑negative conclusions. The plan must reconcile the annotation coverage requirement with the power analysis, either by ensuring human scores for the full 1 000 prompts or by adjusting the sample size/power calculations accordingly.

responses.response: Clarified that we will collect human feasibility scores for **all 1 000 prompts**, satisfying FR‑001 and automatically meeting FR‑009’s minimum of 200.
